newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, NOV 25-SUNDAY, DEC 2.
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, NOV 25-SUNDAY, DEC 2.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS

BRUSSELS - EU foreign ministers meet (Monday-Tuesday); commission report on the state of play on preparation for WTO ministerial conference in Singapore and eighth inter-governmental conference (Monday); structured dialogue with Cyprus (Tuesday).
BRUSSELS - EU consumers ministers meet (Monday); public hearing on protection of consumers interests in the information society.
DUBLIN - Irish Presidency hosts tenth annual European finance convention (Monday-Friday).

BRUSSELS - EU internal market ministers meet (Tuesday); open debate on Commission report on the impact and efficiency of the single market and in margins of the Council ministers will attend the launch of the information campaign on "Citizens Europe".
BRUSSELS - European Commission President Santer and Commissioner Monti hold joint news conference on "Citizens first" (Tuesday).
BRUSSELS - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (Wednesday); presentation on communications on universal telecoms services, postal services and competition in telecoms.
BRUSSELS - European Parliament mini-session (Wednesday-Thursday); report on "Preparation for the third phase of EMU" (Wednesday).
BRUSSELS - Economic and Social Committee holds plenary session (Wednesday-Thursday).
BRUSSELS - EU justice and home affairs ministers meet (Thursday-Friday).

BRUSSELS - EU telecoms ministers meet (Thursday); discussion on the application of an open network provision to vocal telephony and the establishment of a universal telecoms service in a competitive environment.
BRUSSELS - European Commissioners Flynn, Monti and MEP Simone Veil hold joint news conference on the interim report on free movement of persons implied in complementary pensions (Thursday).
BRUSSELS - EU senior veterinary officials meet to review plan to ban the use of suspect sheep tissue in human and animal food (Friday).
MONDAY, NOVEMBER 25
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - General Affairs Council (1000/0900 GMT) (and Tuesday).
- Trade questions:
* Commission report on the state of play on preparation for WTO ministerial conference in Singapore;
* Accession of China to the WTO.
- Situation in former Yugoslavia.
- Peace process in the Middle East.
- Future relations with Turkey.
- Situation in Zaire and the Great Lakes Region.
- Situation in east Timor.
- Seat of the Community Plant Variety Office.
- (1600/1500 GMT) Inter-govermental conference (IGC)
- Exchange of views with EP President Klaus Haensch and MEPs Elmar Brok and Elisabeth Guigou followed by the eighth ministerial meeting.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Consumers Council (1000/0900 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- Consumer access to justice:
* Orientation debate on the suspension of protection on consumer's interest;
* Council conclusion on an access plan for consumers to justice and regulation of consumption differences in the internal market.
- Proposal for directive modifying directive 87/102/EEC on the legislation, regulatory and administrative approximation of consumer credits in member states.
- Commission green paper on financial services: responding to consumer interest.
- (1200/1100 GMT) Public hearing on protection of consumers interest in the information society.
- Exchange of views on the presidency's note on vulnerable consumers and the internal market.
- Commission green paper on trade a communication in the internal market.
- Commission presentation on sale and guarantee of consumption goods.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Brittan meets Indian Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah.

BRUSSELS - European Commission hosts conference on "Investment and trade cooperation between India and the EU" (0800/0700 GMT) (and Tuesday). Speakers include: European Commissioner Marin. Venue: Sheraton Hotel. Contact: Euro Synergy Network (322) 510 2463.
BRUSSELS - European Commission hosts "EITC'96 - Doing business in the information society" conference (0900/0800 GMT) (to Wednesday). Venue: Palais des Congres. Contact: Steve Rogers (322) 296 6613.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1500/1400 GMT) Legal Affairs;
Regional Policy;
Fisheries;
Rules of Procedure;
Women's Rights;
Petitions.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Independant Unions Confederation hold second congress on "The role of unions in a changing society" (and Tuesday). Venue: WTC President Hotel. Contact: CESI (322) 735 5383.

BRUSSELS - The European Women's Lobby (EWL) and Women in Development in Europe (WIDE) hold joint conference on "Alternative economics - The role of women" (2000/1900 GMT). Venue: Amazone conference Room, 10 rue du Meridien. Contact: Barbara Helfferich (322) 217 9020.

BRUSSELS - Brussels Institute for Management of the Environment (IBGE), European Federation of Regional Energy and Environment Agencies (FEDARENE) and Eurocities hold joint conference on "Plans and strategies for waste management at regional and local level" (0900/0800 GMT). Venue: General de Banque auditorium. Contact: IBGE by fax (322) 775 7679.

DUBLIN - Irish Presidency hosts tenth annual European finance convention (to Friday). Agenda includes: the Irish EU presidency; EU regional policy and the single currency. Speakers include: European Commissioner Wulf-Mathies; Irish Central Bank Governor Maurice O'Connell; Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring; European Commission President Jacques Santer. Venue: Shelbourne Hotel. Contact: Tanguy de Craecker (322) 733 5940.
PORTUGAL (NEW ITEM) - NATO Secretary General Javier Solana on official visit; meets Portuguese Prime Minister Prime Minister Antonio Guterres and Defence Minister Antonio Vitorino.
TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 26
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EU foreign ministers hold structured dialogue with Cyprus at 1130/1030 GMT.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Internal Market Council (0930/0830 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- Commission report on the impact and efficiency of the single market - open debate on the Commission's report.
- SLIM initiative: programme evaluation - debate.
- Common position on the modified EP and Council proposal on legal protection of designs and models.
- Free movement of persons, proposals for:
* Council directive suppressing the control of persons at internal borders;

* EP and Council directive modifying October 15, 1968 Council directive 68/360/EEC on the suppression of restrictions on the movement and residence of workers and their families in the EU and May 27, 1973 Council directive 73/148/EEC suppressing restrictions on the movement and residence of member states citizens in the EU regarding establishment and offering of services;
* Council directive on citizens right to travel in the Community.
- Status of the European society:

* Modified proposal for Council regulation on the status of the European society and modified proposal for Council directive completing the status of the European society concerning placing of workers.
- Commission presentation on the "Robert Schuman" action.
- Commission information on the free movement of tour guides and ski teachers from another member state.
- Public procurement - proposal for EP and Council directive:
* Modifying directive 92/50/EEC on the coordination of public procurement procedures for services, directive 93/36/EEC on the coordination of public procurement procedures for public works;
* Modifying directive 93/38/EEC on the coordination of public procurement procedures in the water, energy, transport and telecoms sector;
- Human foodstuff:
* Proposal for directive on third modification of directive 88/344/EEC on the approximation of member states' legislation on extracts used in the fabrication of foodstuff and their ingredients.

- In margins of the Council ministers will attend the launch of the information campaign on "Citizens Europe" at 1300/1200 GMT in the EP building; EP President Klaus Haensch and European Commission President Santer attend.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer and Commissioner Monti hold joint news conference on "Citizens first" (1200/1100 GMT).

LUXEMBOURG - European Commission DG XI hosts standing conference on "Health and safety in the nuclear age: informing the public on European radiation standards" (1030/0930 GMT) (and 27/11). Topics include: major changes in the Euratom basic safety standards directive. Venue: Jean Monnet building, room M6. Contact: Mrs Eisen, DG IX (352) 4301 33 164.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (0900/0800 GMT) Legal Affairs;
Regional Policy;
Fisheries;
Rules of Procedure;
Women's Rights;
Petitions;
- (1100/1000 GMT) Inquiry into Fraud in Transit;
- (1500/1400 GMT) Legal Affairs;
Women's Rights.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Foreign trade Association (FTA) holds news conference on "EU antidumping policy" (1030/0930 GMT). Venue: Hotel Palace. Contact: FTA by fax (322) 762 7506.

BRUSSELS - Civil Society Permanent Forum holds conference on "First civil society states general - Europe for all?" (0900/0800 GMT). Speakers include: MEP Elmar Brok. Venue: Theatre du Residence Palace. Contact: Civil Society Permanent Forum (322) 512 4444.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds seminar on "Managing consumer credit in the EU" (0845/0745 GMT). Main issues discussed are the economic environment; market developments in the EU; the regulatory environment in the EU and the U.S. Venue: CEPS. Contact: Isabelle Tenaerts, CEPS (322) 229 3956.
WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 27
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (0900/0800 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- European Commissioners Bangemann and Van Miert communications on universal telecoms services, postal services and competition in telecoms.
- European Commissioner Bjerregaard communication on environment agreements.
- European Commissioner Bjerregaard communication on the introduction into the EU of furs and products from certain wild animal species.
- European Commissioner Flynn communication on the European observatory for racism and xenophobia.
- European Commissioner Monti communication on a guide to the internal market.
- European Commissioner Van Miert communication on mergers of businesses.
- European Commissioners Papoutsis and Gradin on the fight against sex tourism involving children.
- European Commissioner Fischler on the tobacco market.
- European Commissioner Flynn on the fight against addiction to smoking.
- European Commissioner van den Broek communication on an interim agreement with Azerbaijan.
- European Commissioner Flynn and Commission President Santer communication on structural policy between 1997-1999.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Pinheiro attends emergency debate on the Great Lakes Region. Venue: European Parliament.
BRUSSELS - European Parliament mini-session (and Thursday).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (1500/1400 GMT) Commission communication on urgent political and urgent matters.
- (1630/1530 GMT) Economic Committee recommendation on extending EMI Chairman Alexandre Lamfalussy's mandate.
- Economic Committee recommendation on the nomination of EMI Chairman as of July 1, 1997.
- Joint debate:
- (possibly) Alman Metten report on convergence;
- (possibly) Efthymios Christodoulou report on convergence strengthening during EMU (Stability pact);
- (possibly) Fernand Herman report on regulatory aspects of the introduction of the single currency;
- Karsten Hoppenstedt report on "Preparation for the third phase of EMU".
- (possibly) Claude Desama report on European technological research perspectives to 21st century.
- Florus Wijsenbeek report on Commission's green paper on "Citizens network: public transport for passengers".
- (possibly) Spalato Bellere report on EP and Council eighth directive on summer time COM(96)106.
- Thomas Meghany report on parking cards for disabled persons.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - The Greens in the European Parliament hold news conference on "Europe: priority to social union and policy - an urgency for the inter-governmental conference (IGC)" (1030/0930 GMT). Venue: EP, Espace Leopold press room. Contact: The Greens in the European Parliament (322) 228 42742.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - MEPs Karl von Wogau and Christa Randzio-Plath hold joint news conference following the debate on EMU (1800/1700 GMT).
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (1430/1330 GMT) (and Thursday).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Convention for the protection of the Danube.
- Extraction solvents used in foodstuff.
- Use of airplanes under annex 16 of the international civil aviation convention.
- Sales of goods, guarantees and after-sales support.
- Green paper on commercial communications in the internal market.
- Communication on "Competitiveness of sub-contracting in the textile and clothing industry".
- Common regulations for the international transport of persons by coach and buses.
- Telematic systems in intermodal transport in Europe.
- Fishing vessels safety.
- Equal rights for the disabled.
- Community legislation for energy.
- Organisation of veterinary control on products from third countries.
- European veterinary and plant health agency.
- Sanitary police managing exchanges and imports against pathogenics.
- EU/Canada relations.
- Future of social protection: framework for a European debate.
- Information society: from Corfu to Dublin - preparation for new steps.
- Protection of forests against pollution in the atmosphere and fire.
- Consequences for employment of the introduction on new technologies.
- Identification, registration and labelling system for beef and beef products.

BRUSSELS - European Centre for Advanced Research in Economics (ECARE) holds lunchtime meeting on "European Economic Union: when will it happen and who will join?" (1330/1230 GMT). Venue: ECARE, 39 avenue Franklin Roosevelt. Contact: Nancy De Munck, ECARE (322) 650 3075.
BRUSSELS - European Chemical Industry Council holds economic news conference (1030/0930 GMT). Venue: Hotel Le Meridien. Contact: CEFIC (322) 676 7211.
VENICE - Second ministerial conference on the management of fish stocks in the Mediterranean (to Friday).
THE HAGUE - Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres on official visit to the Netherlands.
THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 28
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Justice and Home Affairs Council (and Friday).
Agenda includes:
- Asylum and immigration:
* Draft joint action on a uniform residence visa;
* Draft recommendation on reception of asylum seekers;
* For information: external borders convention.
- Organised crime:
* 1995 report;
* Implementation of the fight against organised crime.
- Drugs:
* Draft European Council report on drugs - aspects linked to the third pillar;
* Draft joint action on approximation of member state legislation and practices in the fight against drug consumption and traffic.
- Draft resolution on sentences for serious infractions in drug traffic.
- Draft resolution on measures for fighting narcotourism: narcotourism study.
- Draft resolution on measures to combat and dismantle illegal cultivation and production of drugs in member states.
- EDU-Europol - State of work.
- Draft convention on the signature and notification in member states of judicial and extrajudicial acts on civil and trade matters.
- Crime prevention activities - report.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Telecoms Council (1000/0900 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- Council resolution on illegal and harmful content on the Internet.
- Proposal for EP and Council directive on the application of an open network provision to vocal telephony and the establishment of a universal telecoms service in a competitive environment.
- Proposal for EP and Council directive on common rules for the development of Community postal services and the improvement of quality of service.
- Commission presents state of play on WTO/GATS negotiations on basic telecoms.
- Commission information on potential health risks linked to mobile communications.
- Commission presentation on action plan II "Towards the information society in Europe".
- Satellite communications
* Commission information on the follow-up to the informal "ministers and industry" meeting held in Paris October 10, 1996.
- Commission presentation on the green paper on numbering.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioners Flynn and Monti and MEP Simone Veil hold joint news conference on the interim report on free movement of persons involving supplementary pensions (1215/1115 GMT).
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament mini-session (second of two days).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (until 0930/0830 GMT) Political group meetings.
- (EXPANDED ITEM) (0930/0830 GMT) Friedrich Wolf report on employment in Europe - European Commissioner President Santer and Commissioner Flynn attend.
- (1100/1000 GMT) Votes on reports under cooperation, codecision and assent procedures; other motions for resolutions on which debate has closed.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (0900/0800 GMT) (second of two days).

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime seminar on "Environmental policy and its economic aspects" (1315/1215 GMT). Speaker is DG XI Director General Mairus Enthoven. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.

BRUSSELS - "EVA'96 - Electronic Imaging and The Visual Arts" - exchange of experiences, results and loans between EC cultural systems projects. This day will be devoted to providing information about the various programmes and sharing experiences between DG III, X, XII, XIII. Venue: Hotel Palace. Contact: Vasari Ltd. (44) 1252 350780.

BRUSSELS - Paris Institute of Criminology (ICP) and International Group for Research and Information on Security (IGRIS) hold joint conference on "Europe horizon 2000: new threats, new terrorisms". Contact: Fransisco Galvez, IGRIS (322) 511 6428.

BRUSSELS - European Institute for Asian Studies (EIAS) holds conference on "Asian-European trade cooperation in a WTO context" (1045/0945 GMT) (and Friday). Agenda includes: scope for Asia-EU cooperation; implementation of the Uruguay Round; current WTO services negotiations; investment and WTO; environment and WTO; a panel discussion on Euro-Asian trade cooperation. Speakers include: European Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan. Venue: Conrad Hotel. Contact: EIAS, Kerstin Bergloef (322) 230 8122.

LOUVAIN-LA-NEUVE, Belgium - European Studies Institute Chairman Michel Dumoulin hosts conference on "Sound flexibility to achieve European Monetary Union and Portugal's convergence process" (1830/1730 GMT). Speaker is former Portuguese Prime Minister Anibal Antonion Cavaco Silva. Venue: UCL - Auditoire Socrate, 10 Place Cardinal Mercier.

BRUGES, Belgium - European Society of Transport Institutes (ESTI) holds conference on "The citizens' network" (and Friday). Topics discussed include: the implications of external costs principles on urban transport; the network benefits principles; modernising of the regulatory framework in public transport. Venue: Castle Prinsenhof. Contact: Laetitia Hoste, ESTI (322) 230 0514.

LEIPZIG, Germany - Verband Saechssicher Bildungsinstitute hold conference on "Education 2000" (to Saturday). Topics include: the European education market; training in the latest skills; multimedia ability for both suppliers and users; innovation through personal development. Contact: Verband Saechssicher Bildungsinstitute, Dieter Webner (49) 341 490 5910.
LONDON - Agra Europe holds fifth annual European sugar, sweeteners and starch conference (and Friday). Contact: Agra Europe (44) 1892 511 807.
FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 29
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EU senior veterinary officials meet to review plan to ban the use of suspect sheep tissue in human and animal food.
DUBLIN (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer and Commissioner Flynn attend social dialogue summit.
BRUSSELS - European Commission hosts conference on "The role of the media in the peace process in Ex-Yugoslavia" (0930/0830 GMT). Speakers include: MEPs Leo Tindemans, Jan-Willem Bertens.

BRUSSELS - European Parliament hosts conference on "Europe and its nations - before Maastricht II". Participants include: European Commission President Jacques Santer and Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene.
SATURDAY, NOVEMBER 30

LUXEMBOURG - Union of European Federalists (UEF) holds conference on "Euro for employment: a confidence pact" (0900/0800 GMT). Speakers include: MEPs Vivane Reding, Ben Fayot, European Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy and ETUC Confederal Secretary Peter Coldrick. Venue: Jean Monnet building. Contact: UEF (322) 512 1012.
SUNDAY, DECEMBER 1
No events scheduled.
